## My Reasoning

I've been farming in Quzhou my whole life. My father did it, my neighbors do it, and I know this land. Here in Quzhou, everyone grows **winter wheat then summer maize** on the same fields — one after the other, year after year. That's what I'll do again this year on my 8 mu.

I don't know much about vegetables or cash crops, and I don't have connections to sell them at a good price. Wheat in June, corn in October — the county buyers always come, and the government grain subsidy helps. That's reliable income. I won't take risks with something unfamiliar.

**Wheat (October to June):** I'll buy improved seed from the village seed shop — probably 石麦15 or whatever the shop is pushing this year. Before sowing I'll rotary till once, apply compound fertilizer as base, then top-dress urea at jointing. I'll irrigate four times: sowing water, wintering water, jointing, and heading. My neighbor skips the heading water but I don't want to risk it — if there's a dry spell, yields drop badly. I'll spray herbicide in November and fungicide twice in spring for rust and powdery mildew.

**Maize (June to October):** Right after the wheat combine leaves the field, I seed maize with no-till directly — there's no time to plow. I use hybrid seed,郑单958 or similar, same as everyone here. Summer rains usually help but I'll irrigate twice in case July goes dry. One herbicide spray early, one insecticide if I see corn borers.

I won't change what works. Eight mu, two crops, done.
